card.title: Free fall
card.body: Vertical motion under **gravity alone**, with air resistance ignored. Near Earth's surface, every object in free fall — regardless of mass — has the same constant downward **gravitational acceleration** $g \approx 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$. This includes objects dropped, thrown downward, or thrown straight upward.
card.says: once an object leaves your hand and air drag is negligible, gravity pulls it downward at constant acceleration $g$ — even at the very top of a toss where $v = 0$.
card.from: applying the uniform acceleration equations along the vertical axis with $a = g$ downward.
card.useWhen: an object is dropped or thrown vertically and air resistance can be neglected. Choose one positive direction (up or down) and keep the signs of $u$, $v$, $s$, and $g$ consistent.
card.example: Drop a stone from rest ($u = 0$) with $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$ for $t = 3\text{ s}$: velocity $v = 0 + 9.8(3) = 29.4\text{ m/s}$ downward, and distance fallen $h = \dfrac{1}{2}(9.8)(3^2) = 4.9 \times 9 = 44.1\text{ m}$.
card.analogy: In a vacuum tube, a feather and a bowling ball released together fall side by side and hit the bottom at the exact same instant.
